## Plain replay skips execution-refusal integrity validation

**Hosted reproduced regression plus exact-source evidence**, PR #39 head `a59ee77cfa3e57c5bd6ac4d49d8b066f25b4138c`. This is not a claim about a published package or deployed consumer.

`replayRlm` removed unconditional `validateRecorded()` and now invokes it only when `state.components` or `state.reuse_identity` is present. Ordinary runs have neither. Their traversal skips recorded refusals without comparing their code/reason to the actual action outcome.

- [Current replay entry point](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/blob/a59ee77cfa3e57c5bd6ac4d49d8b066f25b4138c/src/engine.ts#L480-L524)
- [Existing regression fixture](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/blob/a59ee77cfa3e57c5bd6ac4d49d8b066f25b4138c/test/review-r6.test.ts#L38-L70)
- [Node 22 failure](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/actions/runs/40749366895/job/123031608027)
- [Node 26 failure](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/actions/runs/40749366895/job/123031608556)

Reproduction on the stated source head, after its normal dependency setup: `node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-name-pattern="review r6 replay rejects altered aggregate and read execution refusals" test/review-r6.test.ts`. This uses the existing synthetic fixture; no external model is needed.

The existing `review r6 replay rejects altered aggregate and read execution refusals` test uses a real SDK scratch tracker and deterministic model, creates a successful plain run with sum/get refusals, replaces a saved refusal reason/code through the checkpoint fixture, then expects replay rejection before inference or history writes. Both jobs fail with `Missing expected rejection.` Related existing legacy/spawn/scope refusal-tampering tests fail the same way. Resume counterparts pass; this finding is specifically the read-only replay validation boundary. Both jobs report 462/485 tests passing; 23 failures include subtests and their containing parent, not 23 independent product defects.

Expected: ordinary replay authenticates execution-refusal records as well as successful reads and final answers, without extra model calls or tracker writes. Actual: a forged refusal can be accepted in a successful plain replay. This weakens durable-history verification and means successful replay no longer attests the refusal transcript promised by existing tests.

The [current accepted implementation record](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/blob/a59ee77cfa3e57c5bd6ac4d49d8b066f25b4138c/.agents/pm/features/pm-rlm-repair-runs.toon) includes native replay in the shared-boundary audit and explicitly retains old assertions/thresholds. Preserving historical read-only compatibility should not bypass refusal verification.

Acceptance:
- Restore equivalent execution-refusal verification for plain replay, preserving legitimate legacy placeholder, read and accounting compatibility.
- Cover both plain and component/reuse-identity modes so stronger opt-in validation does not weaken the default path.
- Reject forged code, reason, missing modern reason and spawn/refusal provenance before a successful result; preserve unchanged source history and zero inference.
- Pass existing review-r6/r7/r8 and evidence/spawn regressions unchanged, with fixed/reverted/restored proof and final-head Node22/26 gates.
- Keep separate proof-target maintenance (#38) and SDK dead-writer recovery (unbraind/pm-cli#1609) independent.

Limits: independently inspected hosted exact-head logs/source, not a new local end-to-end SDK or crash/concurrency reproduction. All 41 all-status issue/PR records and current PR conversation/review records checked; no existing runtime issue matches. Related #38 covers behavioral proof targeting, not this returned-success validation gap.
